question.prompt:
Suppose that \(S\) is a finite set of positive integers.

If the greatest integer in \(S\) is removed from \(S,\) then the average value (arithmetic mean) of the integers remaining is \(32.\) If the least integer in \(S\) is also removed, then the average value of the integers remaining is \(35.\) If the greatest integer is then returned to the set, the average value of the integers rises to \(40.\) The greatest integer in the original set \(S\) is \(72\) greater than the least integer in \(S.\)

What is the average value of all the integers in the set \(S?\)

solutions.title: Compare groups of the same size
solutions.explanation:
Removing only the greatest integer or only the least integer leaves groups of the same size. Comparing their means will therefore reveal how many integers each group contains.

The group with mean \(40\) is obtained from the group with mean \(32\) by replacing the least integer with the greatest integer. This increases the sum by \(72\) and the mean by \(40-32=8\). Since sum equals mean times number of integers, each group contains
\[
\frac{72}{8}=9
\]
integers. The original set therefore contains \(10\) integers.

Removing both extremes leaves eight integers with total
\[
8\cdot35=280.
\]
Removing only the greatest leaves nine integers with total \(9\cdot32=288\). The difference is the least integer, so it equals
\[
288-280=8.
\]
Finally, the nine integers remaining when only the least is removed have total \(9\cdot40=360\). Returning the least integer gives the original total \(360+8=368\).

The average of the original set is
\[
\frac{368}{10}=\boxed{36.8},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

solutions.title: Compare totals of equally sized subsets
Solve for the size and extremes together
